  S s_sample_brief          deliverables/sample-request/sample-creative-brief.json
  S s_sample_criteria       deliverables/sample-request/sample-criteria.json
  S s_sample_request_review deliverables/sample-request/request-review.json
  S s_continuation_5        deliverables/continuation-2026-11-15d.md
  N handoff_6               rv 10, nx [t_sample], bl [t_scout, t_medic, t_family]
No I status/value, C, F, Q, T, X, E, V, D or P change. Encodes work/rev10.json -> work/rev10.px.
The commit is performed separately against the revision 9 hash.

Run from the consumer root with the selected interpreter:  python -I work/build_rev10.py
"""
import hashlib, json, subprocess, sys

PY = sys.executable
RUNNER = "pixl-kit/scripts/pixl.py"
AT = "2026-11-15"
EXPECT_REV = 9
EXPECT_HASH = "fdf4ebfe7d2dc1565a9c003c28d61ecfa5b255ec19937198aa11d405c38b8ca1"
NEW_SOURCES = {
    "s_sample_brief": "deliverables/sample-request/sample-creative-brief.json",
    "s_sample_criteria": "deliverables/sample-request/sample-criteria.json",
    "s_sample_request_review": "deliverables/sample-request/request-review.json",
    "s_continuation_5": "deliverables/continuation-2026-11-15d.md",
}
OUT_JSON, OUT_PX = "work/rev10.json", "work/rev10.px"


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest()


def lines(p):
    return open(p, "rb").read().count(b"\n")


def sym(s):
    return {"$symbol": s}


def ref(s):
    return {"$ref": s}


def refs(*a):
    return [ref(x) for x in a]


def main():
    cur = json.loads(subprocess.run([PY, RUNNER, "decode", "state.px/state.px"],
                                    capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
    assert cur["revision"] == EXPECT_REV, cur["revision"]
    assert sha("state.px/state.px") == EXPECT_HASH, "head bytes drifted"
    R = cur["records"]
    by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in R}
    for new_id in (*NEW_SOURCES, "handoff_6"):
        assert new_id not in by_id, new_id
    before = json.dumps(R, sort_keys=True)

    for sid, path in NEW_SOURCES.items():
        assert lines(path) >= 1, path
        R.append({"id": sid, "kind": "S", "fields": {
            "ur": path, "dg": sha(path), "ln": [1, lines(path)], "at": AT, "au": sym("local")}})

    R.append({"id": "handoff_6", "kind": "N", "fields": {
        "wh": ref("actor"),
        "fo": refs("s_continuation_5", "s_sample_brief", "s_sample_criteria",
                   "s_sample_request_review", "s_continuation_4", "s_eval_answers",
                   "c_sample", "f_sample", "i_outline", "i_canvas", "i_palette",
                   "i_design_language", "i_backgrounds", "i_display_scale", "i_role_diff",
                   "i_animation", "i_engine", "x_aid", "x_study"),
        "nx": refs("t_sample"),
        "bl": refs("t_scout", "t_medic", "t_family"),
        "rv": 10}})

    # every pre-existing record is byte-for-byte the same object as before
    assert json.dumps(R[: len(R) - 5], sort_keys=True) == before
    json.dump({"revision": 10, "records": R, "format": 2},
              open(OUT_JSON, "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
    subprocess.run([PY, RUNNER, "encode", OUT_JSON, "--out", OUT_PX], check=True)
    print("encoded", OUT_PX, "with", len(R), "records")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Continuation note, 2026-11-15 (d): pre-discovery sample request packet and local check tooling

Cold resume of the scout and medic family project by PIXL (agent) in an isolated development
evaluation, assigned by a calling agent. No generation provider, official PixelLab tool, game
engine or network was available or used. Nothing was generated; no provider job exists; no
candidate, evidence or verdict was created; no task state changed; no intake status or value
moved; the two accepted research candidates (`x_study`, `x_aid`) and their verdicts are
untouched. Earlier notes (2026-11-14, 2026-11-15, 2026-11-15b, 2026-11-15c) are preserved
unchanged. This session's consumer root is
`C:/Users/ryanf/AppData/Local/Temp/pixl caller review e3c7ebe124824b69828309bf1645f322/consumer`,
the kit is `pixl-kit/` inside it, and the interpreter is
`C:/github/pixel-lab-agent/.venv/Scripts/python.exe` (Python 3.14.3, Pillow 12.3.0,
jsonschema 4.26.0). Paths in older notes and scripts are provenance only.

## State identity on entry

- `state.px/state.px`: PX2, revision 9, canonical state hash
  `fdf4ebfe7d2dc1565a9c003c28d61ecfa5b255ec19937198aa11d405c38b8ca1`, 71 records, valid, all
  bound files verified (`pixl_workflow`, `pixl_ready`, `pixl_jobs`, focused
  `pixl_context(t_sample, authoring)` this session). `handoff_5` is the current N record.
- Ready: `[t_sample]`, no blockers. `t_scout`, `t_medic`: `task_prerequisite`, `output_contract`,
  `task_decision`. `t_family`: two prerequisites and a decision blocker. No jobs. No families.
- Re-hashed this session, all matching their S records: `sources/brief.md` (`a78aca77...4cf5324`),
  `sources/controlled-evaluation-answers.md` (`87cf7eec...52f6e30`),
  `sources/reference-observations.md` (`d0862d14...a960495`), `sources/method-research.md`
  (`1b1503b7...794e51`), `reference.png` (`d997cade...70aa7`), `reference-b.png`
  (`e76b40ce...14a12a`), the four earlier continuation notes.
- Both references re-measured with `pixl_asset_check`: 32 x 32, 390 visible pixels, zero
  fractional-alpha pixels, one opaque component, visible bbox `[7, 3, 25, 28]` (half-open);
  reference.png 3 colours, reference-b.png 2 colours, none outside
  `#56B5BC / #F4DDA2 / #25354A`. Both 12x views under `work/reference-views/` were viewed: the
  navy in reference.png forms the full contour, both stalks, the shoulder bar and the base
  bar; reference-b.png is the same mask in flat teal with the cream eyes only. Matches the study.

## State identity on exit

- Revision 10, 76 records (71 + `s_sample_brief`, `s_sample_criteria`,
  `s_sample_request_review`, `s_continuation_5`, `handoff_6`), committed to the store folder
  `state.px` with expected hash `fdf4ebfe...8ca1`.
- The revision 10 canonical hash is not written here: this note's own digest is bound by
  `s_continuation_5` inside revision 10. Read it from `state.px/state.px`, its copy in
  `state.px/history/<hash>.px`, `SESSION.md`, or the caller return of this session.
- Expected after commit (no I/C/F/Q/T change, so the lifecycle report cannot differ): ready
  `[t_sample]`; `t_sample` blockers `[]`; production and delivery blockers exactly as on entry.
  `work/verify_rev10.py` checks this against the committed head.

## Owner decisions and authorization, recovered separately from predecessor proposals

- Owner (brief, 2026-09-14, `sources/brief.md`): roster scout + medic (confirmed); side-view game
  (confirmed); the two references are the style authority and disagree about outline; the final
  canvas size is explicitly not chosen; scope "begin the project and make the progress possible
  in this session". That scope is the standing authorization for sample work.
- Controlled-evaluation input (`sources/controlled-evaluation-answers.md`, 8 lines): outlined as
  reference.png (line 5) and 32 x 32 (line 6), for the representative sample only; explicitly not
  an owner preference, not family/production policy, not human acceptance (line 8). Applied in
  revision 9 as `proposed`. No new owner answers exist in this session and none were invented.
- Predecessor proposals (PIXL, not owner): design language (style swatch, side-view figure),
  nearest sampling, facing right, the identity-landmark list, palette exclusivity for the
  sample. All remain proposals; nothing in this session promotes them.
- Not authorized or possible: paid, remote, network or host-configuration actions.

## What was done and why

**(a) Pre-discovery request packet** under `deliverables/sample-request/`. The next operation
(`job-prepare` for `t_sample`) needs the live PixelLab declaration, which this host does not
expose. Everything that does not depend on that declaration was prepared so that the future
translation is a mechanical step against a reviewed contract rather than fresh interpretation:

1. `sample-creative-brief.json`: provider-neutral translation of `c_sample` with `kind`
   `creative_brief`, `executable: false`. The intent is `c_sample.li` verbatim plus a
   component table in which each component keeps its authority wording (observed / PIXL
   proposal / controlled-evaluation sample confirmation / scoped specialist choice; nothing
   called confirmed). Hard constraints: 32 x 32, binary alpha, nearest (as a delivery rule, not
   a generation parameter), single static image, side view, facing right, the three-colour
   working palette, the outlined treatment. Reference roles per `pixellab-operations.md`:
   `reference.png` = style (primary anchor) + palette (sample working set; observed, not
   adopted), not identity/pose/layout/mask/motion; `reference-b.png` = style (secondary),
   conditionally included only if the live operation takes more than one style image with
   `reference.png` first, otherwise omitted from the request (its no-outline treatment pulls
   against the treatment under trial) while remaining the review comparison for
   `q_style_match`. Output cardinality 1 with the retain-all / nominate-one rule. Nine schema
   questions (SQ1-SQ9) that must be answered from the live declaration before translation:
   fixed 32 x 32 output, style-image count and transport, transparency and binary-vs-fractional
   alpha, output count, single-image vs character operation, intent field and parameter-level
   controls, forced palette, poll/retrieve tool, cost.
2. `sample-criteria.json`: validates against `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/asset-plan.schema.json`
   (version 1, scope, one output `f_sample`, contract size/palette/view/sampling/alpha/intent,
   the five exact revision 9 criterion texts with id, check, domain, mode, basis, scope,
   authority and sources). Every `lines` bound was verified by opening the file; the retained
   validation output (`criteria-schema-validation.json`) records `schema_valid: true` and all 18
   bounds inside their files. Authority labels: `proposal` for the four `wh=actor` sample
   criteria (each basis splits the observed, evaluation-confirmed and specialist clauses, since
   the schema allows one label per criterion), `requirement` for the owner-owned
   `q_style_match`.
3. `request-review.json` per `request-review.md`: sources with sha256 and locators, `request`
   pointing at the brief with `kind: creative_brief`, `executable: false`, `tool: null`;
   `criteria` with the validation link and the saved Q record hashes; `choices`; `resume`
   (store/task/output/contract/hash); local tooling links. It states that `pixl_request_review`
   cannot consume it: the runtime (`request_review.py` lines 130-134) requires
   `request.kind == "provider_arguments"`. This was demonstrated and retained
   (`request-review-tool-refusal.json`, exit 2, "review expects exact provider arguments, not a
   creative brief"). That refusal is the expected behaviour for a pre-discovery packet, not a
   packet defect; a successor packet with exact provider arguments will be reviewable.

**(b) Operation shortlist** `operation-shortlist.json`, built from `pixl_capabilities` and
labelled as what it is: a documentation catalog retrieved 2026-09-11 with `live_discovery:
false`, supplying names, required argument names and poll tools only. Five plausible rows
(`create_image_pro`, `create_image_pixflux`, `create_image_pixen`, `create_character`,
`create_1_direction_object`) each carry the discriminating questions to put to the live
declaration; post-processing tools and non-applicable tools are listed separately; no tool is
decided. Decision rule: fixed 32 x 32 output, an actual style-image input with usable
transport, transparent output, single-image packaging; otherwise report the mismatch with a
staged path rather than changing the contract.

**(c) Local mechanical check harness** `work/sample-checks/check_sample_mechanical.py`,

"""Validate sample-criteria.json against the kit's asset-plan.schema.json. READ-ONLY by default.

Successor of validate_criteria.py (retained unchanged as the script that produced
criteria-schema-validation.json, sha256 93643a34...). The v1 script wrote that retained
artifact unconditionally on every run, so reproducing the validation as its docstring
instructed overwrote a file whose hash is quoted in bound artifacts (caller finding 1,
2026-11-15e). This version never writes unless an explicit --out path is given, and
refuses to write over an existing file. Reviewers reproducing the validation must use
this script, not v1.

Passing means structural validity against the schema plus file-local line-bound sanity.
It is not a semantic review, not acceptance and not provider-schema validity.

Usage (consumer root, selected interpreter, isolated mode):
  python -I deliverables/sample-request/validate_criteria_v2.py                # print only
  python -I deliverables/sample-request/validate_criteria_v2.py --out NEW.json # also save
  python -I deliverables/sample-request/validate_criteria_v2.py --criteria PATH --schema PATH
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator

DEFAULT_SCHEMA = "pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/asset-plan.schema.json"
DEFAULT_CRITERIA = "deliverables/sample-request/sample-criteria.json"


def sha(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        return hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest()


def report(schema_path, criteria_path):
    schema = json.load(open(schema_path, encoding="utf-8"))
    plan = json.load(open(criteria_path, encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    validator = Draft202012Validator(schema)
    errors = [
        {"path": "/" + "/".join(str(p) for p in e.absolute_path), "message": e.message}
        for e in sorted(validator.iter_errors(plan), key=lambda e: list(e.absolute_path))
    ]
    bounds = []
    for output in plan.get("outputs", []):
        for criterion in output.get("criteria", []):
            for source in criterion.get("sources", []):
                if "lines" in source:
                    with open(source["path"], "rb") as handle:
                        total = handle.read().count(b"\n")
                    first, last = source["lines"]
                    bounds.append({
                        "criterion": criterion["id"], "path": source["path"],
                        "lines": source["lines"], "file_lines": total,
                        "in_bounds": 1 <= first <= last <= total,
                    })
    return {
        "validated_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "validator": "jsonschema.Draft202012Validator",
        "script": "deliverables/sample-request/validate_criteria_v2.py",
        "schema": {"path": schema_path, "sha256": sha(schema_path)},
        "criteria": {"path": criteria_path, "sha256": sha(criteria_path)},
        "schema_valid": not errors,
        "errors": errors,
        "line_bounds": bounds,
        "all_line_bounds_inside_files": all(b["in_bounds"] for b in bounds),
        "meaning": "Structural validity against asset-plan.schema.json and file-local bound "
                   "sanity only. Not a semantic review, not acceptance, not provider-schema "
                   "validity. This run wrote nothing unless --out named a fresh path.",
    }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--schema", default=DEFAULT_SCHEMA)
    parser.add_argument("--criteria", default=DEFAULT_CRITERIA)
    parser.add_argument("--out", help="save the report to this NEW path (refuses to overwrite)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.out and os.path.exists(args.out):
        print(json.dumps({"error": f"refusing to overwrite existing file: {args.out}"}))
        return 2
    result = report(args.schema, args.criteria)
    text = json.dumps(result, indent=1)
    print(text)
    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "x", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
            handle.write(text + "\n")
    return 0 if result["schema_valid"] and result["all_line_bounds_inside_files"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Revision 11 (2026-11-15e): bind the successor brief/packet (caller findings 1 and 2) and note.

Appends four records to the revision 10 head and changes nothing else:
  S s_sample_brief_v2           deliverables/sample-request/sample-creative-brief-v2.json
  S s_sample_request_review_v2  deliverables/sample-request/request-review-v2.json
  S s_continuation_6            deliverables/continuation-2026-11-15e.md
  N handoff_7                   rv 11, nx [t_sample], bl [t_scout, t_medic, t_family]
The v1 packet S records (s_sample_brief, s_sample_criteria, s_sample_request_review) stay as
the pre-discovery identity. No I status/value, C, F, Q, T, X, E, V, D or P change.
Encodes work/rev11.json -> work/rev11.px; the commit is performed separately against the
revision 10 hash.

Run from the consumer root with the selected interpreter:  python -I work/build_rev11.py
"""
import hashlib, json, subprocess, sys

PY = sys.executable
RUNNER = "pixl-kit/scripts/pixl.py"
AT = "2026-11-15"
EXPECT_REV = 10
EXPECT_HASH = "23f4ee559508bab7b1966348589c1431604b848b804f7e6599940e48b06968c6"
NEW_SOURCES = {
    "s_sample_brief_v2": "deliverables/sample-request/sample-creative-brief-v2.json",
    "s_sample_request_review_v2": "deliverables/sample-request/request-review-v2.json",
    "s_continuation_6": "deliverables/continuation-2026-11-15e.md",
}
OUT_JSON, OUT_PX = "work/rev11.json", "work/rev11.px"


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest()


def lines(p):
    return open(p, "rb").read().count(b"\n")


def sym(s):
    return {"$symbol": s}


def ref(s):
    return {"$ref": s}


def refs(*a):
    return [ref(x) for x in a]


def main():
    cur = json.loads(subprocess.run([PY, RUNNER, "decode", "state.px/state.px"],
                                    capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
    assert cur["revision"] == EXPECT_REV, cur["revision"]
    assert sha("state.px/state.px") == EXPECT_HASH, "head bytes drifted"
    R = cur["records"]
    by_id = {r["id"]: r for r in R}
    for new_id in (*NEW_SOURCES, "handoff_7"):
        assert new_id not in by_id, new_id
    before = json.dumps(R, sort_keys=True)

    for sid, path in NEW_SOURCES.items():
        assert lines(path) >= 1, path
        R.append({"id": sid, "kind": "S", "fields": {
            "ur": path, "dg": sha(path), "ln": [1, lines(path)], "at": AT, "au": sym("local")}})

    R.append({"id": "handoff_7", "kind": "N", "fields": {
        "wh": ref("actor"),
        "fo": refs("s_continuation_6", "s_sample_brief_v2", "s_sample_request_review_v2",
                   "s_sample_criteria", "s_sample_brief", "s_sample_request_review",
                   "s_continuation_5", "s_eval_answers", "c_sample", "f_sample",
                   "i_outline", "i_canvas", "i_palette", "i_design_language", "i_backgrounds",
                   "i_display_scale", "i_role_diff", "i_animation", "i_engine",
                   "x_aid", "x_study"),
        "nx": refs("t_sample"),
        "bl": refs("t_scout", "t_medic", "t_family"),
        "rv": 11}})

    assert json.dumps(R[: len(R) - 4], sort_keys=True) == before
    json.dump({"revision": 11, "records": R, "format": 2},
              open(OUT_JSON, "w", encoding="utf-8"), indent=1)
    subprocess.run([PY, RUNNER, "encode", OUT_JSON, "--out", OUT_PX], check=True)
    print("encoded", OUT_PX, "with", len(R), "records")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Continuation note, 2026-11-15 (e): corrections after caller review of revision 10

Same session, same isolation and same paths as `deliverables/continuation-2026-11-15d.md`
(retained unchanged, sha256 `826460e5ff96f7dae2bccff8b8df1278e5457614cfaadd3c0510e0f64feeb1dc`,
bound as `s_continuation_5`). The caller reviewed revision 10 independently, verified it
consistent on every claim it checked, accepted the S-record binding of the packet files and the
`deliverables/sample-request/` location, and returned two findings. Both are correct. This note
records the old-to-new correction for each, the files added, and the revision 11 delta. No
generation, provider job, candidate, evidence, verdict, task-state or intake change occurred.
The contract `c_sample`, the five sample criteria and `sample-criteria.json` are untouched.

## State identity on entry

- `state.px/state.px`: PX2, revision 10, canonical state hash
  `23f4ee559508bab7b1966348589c1431604b848b804f7e6599940e48b06968c6`, 76 records, valid, files
  verified. Ready `[t_sample]`, no jobs, no families. `handoff_6` current.
- Retained artifact `deliverables/sample-request/criteria-schema-validation.json` confirmed at
  its quoted hash `93643a34d32353b5471fd9943aed8bb3a0bf8cb48a94d8413c42635a1aaeb16a` after the
  caller's restore (caller script `work/caller-restore-validation.py`, sha256
  `603ede5e838eb8c76312c3666848dd4cd07f1ee68cb21edadb059ce909a64904`, not mine, not edited).

## State identity on exit

- Revision 11, 80 records (76 + `s_sample_brief_v2`, `s_sample_request_review_v2`,
  `s_continuation_6`, `handoff_7`), committed to the store folder `state.px` with expected hash
  `23f4ee55...68c6`. The revision 11 canonical hash is not written here (this note's digest is
  bound inside it); read it from `state.px/state.px`, `SESSION.md` or the caller return.
- Expected after commit: ready `[t_sample]`, blockers unchanged, no jobs.
  `work/verify_rev11.py` checks this against the committed head.

## Finding 1 (reproducibility defect): the v1 validator overwrote a hash-quoted artifact

**Old.** `deliverables/sample-request/validate_criteria.py` (sha256 `48f3d0f1...dbe45`) hard-codes
`OUT` to the retained `criteria-schema-validation.json` and writes it on every run, while its
docstring invites reviewers to run it to reproduce the validation. Doing so rewrites
`validated_at`, changing the artifact's hash, which is quoted in `request-review.json`
(bound `s_sample_request_review`) and in `continuation-2026-11-15d.md` line 141 (bound
`s_continuation_5`). The caller observed exactly this drift (to `82d7df80...765d5`) and
restored the original bytes.

**New.** `deliverables/sample-request/validate_criteria_v2.py` (sha256
`b582f32737eb5733f6be883c3e08b0ce9423408bb7249caa3b7c32d12011719b`): read-only by default
(prints the report); writes only to an explicit `--out` path; opens that path with mode `x`
and refuses to overwrite an existing file (exit 2); accepts `--criteria` / `--schema`
overrides. Demonstrated this session: print-only run (exit 0, `schema_valid true`,
`all_line_bounds_inside_files true`); `--out work/sample-checks/criteria-validation-rerun-v2.json`
(fresh file, sha256 `d22798dcafd78049d59576dc712edeffa48630388a244e7c7fb2bc20a45093bc`); a
second `--out` to the same path refused; the retained artifact still hashed `93643a34...` after
all three runs. `work/verify_rev11.py` repeats the print-only run and fails if the retained
artifact changes.

**Not changed.** `validate_criteria.py` and `criteria-schema-validation.json` keep their bytes:
the v1 script is retained as the one that produced the `93643a34...` artifact. **Instruction
for every reviewer and successor: reproduce the validation only with `validate_criteria_v2.py`;
do not run `validate_criteria.py`.** The v2 packet states the same.

## Finding 2 (mixed authority under one label): brief intent component 3 and wording rules

**Old** (`sample-creative-brief.json`, sha256 `cc21bf77...380ce`, bound `s_sample_brief`,
retained unchanged as the pre-discovery identity). Component 3, labelled "controlled-evaluation
sample confirmation", read: "Outlined as reference.png: a flat #25354A contour at the weight
shown there (2 logical px) fully enclosing the figure, which also forms the shoulder bar, the
base bar and the two solid top stalks, adapted to the side view. The outline colour is the only
dark value; no second outline tone, no selective outlining." The evaluation answer
(`sources/controlled-evaluation-answers.md` line 5) says only "Use the outlined treatment shown
in reference.png." The single-flat-colour fact is a measurement (`sources/reference-observations.md`
lines 37-40, line 40 "Outline is a single flat colour with no ramp"), and "only dark value /
no second outline tone / no selective outlining" is my provider-wording tightening. One label
covered three authorities. Less consequentially, component 1's "no gradients, no dithering"
lacked its locator (line 29, same observed class), and `provider_wording_rules` listed "no drop
shadow" without attributing it as a specialist choice.

**Chosen disposition: (a) a successor brief and packet, bound in revision 11.** Reason: the
brief is the exact text the future `provider_arguments` translation will read. A split recorded
only in a note would have to be re-applied by hand at translation time, which is the same
silent-carry risk the finding identifies; a v2 file makes the split the source. The v1 packet
remains the pre-discovery identity; nothing in it was edited.

**New** (`sample-creative-brief-v2.json`, sha256
`f84b262818bbf044eb22716ab5d02eed1103cc65714360fcfc5d9efd019a5b80`):

| Location | Old (v1) | New (v2) | Authority change |
|---|---|---|---|
| intent component 3 | one clause under "controlled-evaluation sample confirmation" | **3a** the evaluation answer's clause exactly as in `c_sample.li` (sample-scoped confirmation); **3b** what reference.png measurably shows: one flat colour `#25354A`, no ramp or second tone, 2 logical px (observation, lines 37-40); **3c** "no selective outlining; `#25354A` the only dark value; no second outline tone, no inner dark shading" (scoped specialist provider-wording choice, consistent with `c_sample.li` "fully enclosing"; revisable without touching `c_sample`) | none gains authority; the tightening is now attributed to the specialist |
| intent component 1 | "no gradients, no dithering" under observed, no locator for dithering | same text, citing `reference-observations.md` line 29 | none |
| `provider_wording_rules` | flat list; "no drop shadow" unattributed | each rule carries its authority; "no drop shadow" and "outline only in #25354A / no selective outlining / no second tone" labelled scoped specialist choices and added to `specialist_choices_in_this_brief` | attribution corrected |
| `hard_constraints.outline` | authority text mixed | authority text names the three parts (confirmation / measurement / 3c choice) | none |
| `supersedes` block | absent | v1 path, hash, reason, this table | n/a |
| everything else | v1 | unchanged (state binding, deliverable, references, cardinality, SQ1-SQ9, exclusions, acceptance route; `next_operation` now says the then-current hash is revision 11's) | none |

The composed `c_sample.li` string inside the brief is unchanged and still equals the saved
contract field. `q_sample_outline` keeps its revision 9 text; it tests "fully enclosing the
figure ... applied consistently on every contour", which is the required outcome. Component 3c
is wording to help a generator meet that outcome, not a new rejection rule.

`request-review-v2.json` (sha256 `a596f02addb73ba1c7732cfe05a8071b97b7c7236f26e349fdca5184e0684d73`)
points `request` at the v2 brief, keeps `criteria` at the unchanged `sample-criteria.json`

`87f06d6dc0ca49f5398116fb7faf40003db713e66e019a2519f1cb9f90781b65`, exit 2, "review expects
